name: Frankie Levin
occupation: Former drug seller and furniture mover
life: “I still remember moving furniture through a lobby where I used to sell drugs.” On Thursday, near the bank steps, Frankie takes a few minutes to read the public notices, especially the ones written in a hurry.
voice: I used to bring him drugs. He asked me for the number of a furniture mover and nothing else.
appearance: Frankie has a center part and straight chestnut hair, a deep crease beside the mouth when smiling, and a favorite piece of clothing, a faded indigo overshirt. It usually goes with a watch on a cracked leather band. When somebody else has the floor, Frankie raises one eyebrow long before saying yes.
personality: Frankie is kind in very practical ways and prickly about being thanked in public. Frankie loves being recognized by the people who notice what happens after the guests have left.
agenda: To give the father an ordinary contact for moving furniture.
family: Marc Carr is Frankie’s half-sibling. Frankie puts the kettle on. Marc chooses the music. The cups come out before either brings up the reason for the visit. They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *Names on the night wall*, Marc says, “I am the neighbor named in three different cards.”
connections: Evelyn Kaur. A furniture number and a quiet evening may be more usable than a homecoming party.

reactions.response: Frankie gives the child an ordinary excuse to step outside without suggesting they reject the father.
